facts.statement: The genus Dactylosaurus was first described by Gürich in 1884.
Dactylosaurus is classified as a genus of nothosaur within the family Pachypleurosauridae.
facts.quote: Dactylosaurus is a genus of nothosaur in the family Pachypleurosauridae.

facts.statement: The name Dactylosaurus translates to "finger lizard" or "finger reptile" from Greek.
facts.quote: Dactylosaurus comes from the Greek (δακτυλος), "finger" and (σαυρος), meaning "lizard" or "reptile."

facts.statement: Dactylosaurus was a small reptile that grew to a maximum length of 50 cm.
facts.quote: Dactylosaurus was a small reptile measuring up to 50 cm long.

facts.statement: The skeleton of Dactylosaurus included 17 cervical vertebrae with cervical ribs featuring anterior processes.
facts.quote: There are 17 cervical vertebrae and the cervical ribs have anterior processes.

facts.statement: Dactylosaurus gracilis is the smallest known species within its family, Pachypleurosauridae.
facts.quote: D. gracilis is the smallest known species in its family

facts.statement: The single forelimb found on the holotype had a slimmer radius and ulna compared to the similar European nothosaur Neusticosaurus.
facts.quote: The one limb that was found (a left forelimb), was noted to have a slimmer radius and ulna than Neusticosaurus, a similar nothosaur from Europe.

facts.statement: Dactylosaurus lived in central Europe during the Early and Middle Triassic periods, specifically the Late Olenekian and Anisian stages.
facts.quote: Dactylosaurus lived in the Early and Middle Triassic period during the Late Olenekian and Anisian faunal stage, of central Europe.

facts.statement: A new site in Gogolin containing abundant remains of Dactylosaurus was discovered in 2012 and dates to approximately 247 million years ago.
facts.quote: In 2012, the new Röt site (~ 247 Ma; Lower Triassic; the latest Olenekian) with abundant disarticulated remains of Dactylosaurus was found in Gogolin.

facts.statement: Dactylosaurus is classified under the class Reptilia.
